scope: Final independent mathematical review of the integrated Unit 007 canonical reader, covering FOM-PR-13 through FOM-PR-15 and all six edition-original mastery exercise, hint, and solution triples.

repair_closure.evidence: The presentation comparison now says that the transformed standard relator is a cyclic conjugate of (b^2a^2)^{-1}, uses invariance of the normal closure under conjugation and inversion, and explicitly distinguishes the direct chain isomorphism F_1(y)=s, F_2(Delta_std)=Delta from the generator-induced isomorphism F_1(y)=-s, F_2(Delta_std)=-Delta.
The unique 0-cell is consistently v_0 and the new degree-one basis is u=a, s=a+b, eliminating the cross-degree symbol collision.
The skeletal-stabilization display now contains the valid TeX condition H_k(X)\qquad(k<n).
The incidence theorem explicitly assumes n>=1 and types n=1 using X^(0)_+, a disjoint basepoint, and degree on reduced H_0(S^0).

proof_repair_checks.evidence: For r>=n+1 and n>k, r>k+1, so the relative groups in degrees k+1 and k both vanish and adjacent skeleta induce H_k-isomorphisms. Closure-finiteness plus weak topology proves that a compact subset lies in a finite subcomplex. Cycle support gives surjectivity; the joint support of a cycle and a bounding chain gives injectivity. The proof does not invoke cellular homology.

The composition d_n=rho_{n-1}delta_n is typed, and delta_{n-1}rho_{n-1}=0 is the consecutive-map relation in the long exact sequence. Vanishing above skeletal dimension makes rho_n and rho_{n-1} injective, giving ker d_n=im rho_n; rho_0 is the identity and d_0=0. The pair (X^(n+1),X^n), followed by FOM-PR-13, identifies cellular and singular homology. Maps of skeletal pairs prove naturality for cellular maps, and cellular approximation gives the arbitrary-continuous-map statement.

Both incidence spheres have dimension n-1, P_beta collapses precisely the summands delta!=beta, and the outward-normal-first boundary orientation introduces no hidden sign. Coordinate projection after the connecting map yields the stated degree coefficient. The n=1 endpoint incidence is correctly read in reduced H_0(S^0), and compactness of the attaching sphere gives finite support even when the CW complex has infinitely many cells.

mastery_checks.independent_recomputation: Exponent sums give d_2=[[2,1],[-1,2]]. Its determinant is 5 and its Smith form is diag(1,5); therefore ker d_2=0, H_2=0, H_1=Z/5, and H_0=Z.

The long exact sequence proves vanishing above skeletal dimension, an isomorphism below n, and an epimorphism in degree n. Attaching one (n+1)-cell to S^n by the identity gives D^(n+1), proving that the degree-n epimorphism need not be injective. Finite-subcomplex support supplies the arbitrary-CW passage.

The incidence matrix is A=[[1,-2],[0,3],[-1,1]]. Reversing x_1 and e_2 gives A'=PAQ=[[-1,-2],[0,-3],[1,1]]. The two columns are independent; gcd of entries is 1 and gcd of the 2x2 minors 3,-1,3 is 1, so the Smith form has nonzero diagonal 1,1, H_2=0, and H_1=Z.
Every generator has exponent sum zero in the product of commutators and every 1-cell is a loop at the unique vertex, so d_2=d_1=0. Hence H_2=Z, H_1=Z^(2g), H_0=Z, and chi=2-2g.

The source polygon word b^2a^2 has exponent vector (2,2), so d_2(Delta)=2(a+b), ker d_2=0, im d_2=Z(2,2), H_2=0, H_1=Z plus Z/2, and H_0=Z. The unimodular basis u=a, s=a+b sends d_2 to 2s. Under x=a, y=a^{-1}b^{-1}, the standard relator becomes b^{-1}a^{-2}b^{-1}, a cyclic conjugate of (b^2a^2)^{-1}; the two chain isomorphisms and their signs are now distinguished correctly.

The two local degree contributions are 1 and deg(antipodal on S^(k-1))=(-1)^k, so d_k=0 for odd k and multiplication by 2 for even k. Thus positive odd homology below n is Z/2, top homology is Z exactly for odd n, and the displayed RP^4 and RP^5 complexes and homology groups have the correct parity.

final_conclusion: The canonical reader identity reviewed here has no P1, P2, or P3 mathematical findings. FOM-PR-13 through FOM-PR-15 are complete, correctly placed, typed, non-circular, and valid for their stated CW-complex scope; all six mastery triples have correct matrices, Smith reductions, kernel-image calculations, group-presentation comparison, and parity conclusions.
